Work Contracts in Action: Advancing High-performance, Low-latency Concurrency in C++ - Michael Maniscalco - CppCon 2025
---

Real-time systems such as high-frequency trading, game engines, and embedded control demand predictable, low-latency execution. However, conventional C++ task-based concurrency models, including futures, promises, lock-free techniques, MPMC queues, and other synchronization mechanisms, typically introduce coordination overhead and latency, limiting the system's ability to meet performance requirements. 
 
Work Contracts, introduced in 2024, is a lock-free, wait-free C++ concurrency framework engineered to minimize latency by eliminating the contention and coordination overhead inherent in existing task-based concurrency models. Its signal-based task orchestration sidesteps blocking and unnecessary synchronization entirely, enabling fine-grained, non-blocking task dependencies.
